2) Colon suspensions: a colon marks a shortened word; keep it where written: Tho:, Captn:, John:, S:^d, Exec:^rs (colon before the ^). In this sub-class: almost never (<1 %).
3) Ampersand: write & exactly where the scribe wrote an ampersand; never replace it by 'and' (a few hands write a plus-like '+': keep +). In this sub-class: almost never (<1 %).
4) Thorn words: ye, yt, ym, yr (y = th) are written as they appear; never expand to the, that, them, their. In this sub-class: almost never (<1 %).
5) Initial ff: keep a doubled initial ff (ffrancis, ffeb^ry, ffor). In this sub-class: almost never (<1 %).
6) Digits and numbers: copy digits, years and ordinals exactly (1647, 19^th); keep roman numerals and number words as written. In this sub-class: almost never (<1 %).
7) Interlined words and fillers: words inserted above the line are written between tildes (~and~); a ~, _ or - that fills the end of the line is kept. In this sub-class ~ occurs almost never (<1 %), _ almost never (<1 %), and a final - almost never (<1 %).
8) Apostrophes and quotes: an apostrophe or a quote mark used as an abbreviation sign stays: afores'd, p'forme, plantac"on. In this sub-class: almost never (<1 %).
9) Commas and periods: only where the scribe wrote them; never add sentence punctuation. In this sub-class commas occur about one line in 2 (50 %), periods almost never (<1 %).
10) Capitals: copy every capital exactly as written, even inside a sentence (Said, Same, Land); never normalise case. In this sub-class 14 % of the words start with a capital.
11) Spelling: keep the original spelling: heires, assignes, publique, yeare, doe, bee, mee, tenne, heyres, saide; never modernise.
12) Unmarked abbreviations: sd, wch, wth, pte, pish, pmisses, admrs stay exactly as written; never expand. In this sub-class: almost never (<1 %).

HABITS OF THIS SUB-CLASS (from its training lines)
- Superscripts in about three lines in ten and colon + caret suspensions (S:^d, Exec:^rs).
- Commas in about one line in five; '_' may fill the end of the line.
- Old spellings: mee, bee, wee, tenn dayes, conteyneing.
- Words typical of this sub-class, spelled as its scribes wrote them: and, the.
- 'Said' with a capital occurs almost never (<1 %); lower-case 'said' about one line in 4 (25 %): follow the image, not habit.

COMMON MISTAKES TO AVOID IN THIS SUB-CLASS
- The order of colon and caret in suspensions.
- Stopping before the true end of the long line.
- Added or missing commas.

WHAT TO IGNORE
- Ink from the lines above and below, bleed-through from the back of the page, stains, holes, ruling, margins and page edges.
- Do not describe the image. Do not add line numbers, quotes or brackets that are not written.

EXAMPLE TRANSCRIPTIONS FROM THIS SUB-CLASS (ground truth of other training lines)
- Hundred thirty three pounds money to mee in hand paid by Edward Parsons of the
- hereof, the receipt whereof and of every part and parcell thereof wee doe

MANDATORY SILENT RE-CHECK BEFORE OUTPUT
- Every visible word of the central line is present, from the first to the last; nothing from other lines.
- Every ^, :, &, ~, apostrophe and comma that is written is present, in the right place, and none is invented.
- Capitals and spellings are the scribe's, not modern English.

OUTPUT FORMAT (MANDATORY)
Return ONLY the transcription of the line as plain text on one line: no quotes, no labels, no explanations, no markdown.

RETURN ONLY THE TRANSCRIPTION.
